summary: Elliott Nunatak is a large nunatak, a peak of rock protruding through ice, that juts out from the center of the Bermel Escarpment in the Thiel Mountains of Antarctica. It is named after Raymond L. Elliott, a geologist with the United States Geological Survey Thiel Mountains party that surveyed the range in 1960–61. The name was proposed by the party's co-leaders, Peter Bermel and Arthur Ford.
one_line: Elliott Nunatak is a large Antarctic nunatak in the Thiel Mountains, named for USGS geologist Raymond L. Elliott.
